name: Ossavel Sorrel-Yuzu Tonic
description: A mid-range tonic blending sorrel's tart hibiscus-adjacent notes with real yuzu peel oil — one of the few Calder & Voss products to use any real extract at this price point. Sold in slender 280ml glass-composite bottles.
flavor_profile: Sharp citrus bite from yuzu, followed by the cranberry-adjacent tartness of sorrel; quinine bitterness is present but restrained, with a clean mineral finish
cultural_context: A favorite mixer in Tier 2 home bars and Tier 3 casual lounges; bartenders at mid-range establishments use it as a quality signal — ordering Ossavel in a Tier 2 bar marks you as someone who knows drinks.
story_hooks: A batch of Ossavel was contaminated at a Calder & Voss micro-plant in the Lakeward district — the contaminant wasn't accidental, and the plant manager has vanished.
An underground cocktail competition in the Midden uses only Ossavel as the required tonic; the prize is rumored to be a Tier 4 residential pass.
The real yuzu peel in Ossavel is sourced from a single hydroponic collective in the Upper Corridor — that collective just burned down, and the insurance claim doesn't add up.
